documented_native_fact: ARK describes disruptive platforms by steep cost declines, cross-sector reach and capacity to enable additional innovation.
documented_scope: General platform identification; Brett Winton’s published framework, not Cathie Wood’s individual rule set.

precise_locator.paragraphs: Three intrinsic-property paragraphs after the introductory definition

evidence_anchors.supporting_paraphrase: Uses cost, sector reach and enabling-platform properties.
Incumbent displacement is possible, not inevitable.

application_design.authorship: Independent auditor operationalization; not an investor quotation, recovered personal algorithm or claim of historical use.
required_quantitative_inputs: Quality-adjusted cost history and service price
Number and revenue share of distinct addressable use cases/sectors
Active independent developers, deployed complements and paid adoption
research_checks: Document which of the three properties is evidenced and which is only a forecast.
Tie enabling platforms to the actual company’s attainable economics.
falsifiers_or_contrary_mechanisms: Cost declines stall or performance does not meet customer requirements.
Platform complements fail to gain paying adoption; incumbents preserve customer access or economics.
application_limits: A platform-level property does not select a security or establish its value capture.
No automatic technology-sector eligibility; absence of an input is missing evidence, not a positive score.
